finite_assessment.complete_old_expression_basis: The complete1712Ambrosian EasterDay postcommunion already joins perpetual divine favor toward the Church, transformation by the paschal mysteries, and arrival at resurrection radiance in exactly this syntax and order. Precisely two conventional verbs differ. Neither is hidden as spelling or exact old wording; this complete finite adaptation requires individual review. The whole old prayer is retained and its Ambrosianappointment is not relabeled as modernRoman.
exact_changes: Replace prosequere with tuere, changing the request to attend/accompany the Church in loving favor to guard her.
Replace resuscitata with renovata, changing raised/revived to renewed by the paschal mysteries.
Replace the actually printed old Per Dominum nostrum cue with the modern Per Christum cue, using the whole independently old Per Christum Dominum nostrum. R. Amen. formula from PustetAP776.
Mechanically normalize historical u/v, stress accents, ligatures and punctuation. No additional clause or changed word order is supplied.
finite_assessment.translation_notes: Tuere is guard; pio favore is loving favor; renovata is renewed, not old resuscitata. The Church remains the singular subject of reaching resurrection radiance. Perpetuo remains always, and the complete independently old short conclusion and distinct response are rendered.
finite_assessment.strongest_contrary_argument: Two lexical choices can alter a prayer: attending becomes protection and revived becomes renewal. No word-count threshold alone removes the possibility of original modern expression. The favorable finite assessment is that these conventional near-synonymous choices preserve the exact complete old invocation, relative scope, syntax, ordered petition and resurrection outcome without adding a new clause or image. This supports review of only this whole adapted study expression, not clearance of the entire modernMissal.
